fields.Catch source: Sea Around Us regional catch, 1950–2019. Review reference: 2019 total catch, including landings and discards. Retained regional inputs; source release date not recorded.
fields.Selected article: ICES (2016). Report of the Working Group on Multispecies Assessment Methods (WGSAM), 9–13 November 2015. Annex 6, North Sea Key Run, printed pp. 102–206. The deposited Rpath port is a distinct source snapshot; the report is comparison evidence.
fields.Other known articles:
Saygu et al. (2025), Historical ecosystem models can serve as a baseline for indicator-based assessment: the North Sea. Its 1991–1995 Scotland model is compared below.
Mackinson and Daskalov (2007), An ecosystem model of the North Sea to support an ecosystem approach to fisheries management: description and parameterisation.
Mackinson (2014), Building an Ecopath with Ecosim model of the North Sea.
Hill et al. (2021), Modelling the trophic interaction, structure, and function of the northern North Sea food web: Ecopath Technical Report.
Pint et al. (2024), Ecopath model of the Southern Bight of the North Sea (version 3). These inventory sources were not additional full validations.
fields.Selected model: ICES_WGSAM2015_North_Sea_1991. Deposited North Sea Rpath port, static 1991 base state; ICES divisions IVa–IVc. 69 source ecological groups and 11 fleets. Five juvenile/adult stock pairs. The accepted native EwE Key Run database is unavailable.
fields.Other models from the same article: The accepted native configuration named Keyrun 2015_NorthSea1991_12Jan16.eweaccdb differs materially from this port and is not available locally. The contextual 2018 management-plan application has 10 fleets, versus 11 in the deposited port; it is not interchangeable.
fields.Selection rationale:
Article — No separate article-choice rationale is recorded.
Model — The researcher selected this published North Sea 1991 Rpath snapshot on 14/10/2026 because its static mass-balance checks pass. Recorded limitations include its difference from the native EwE Key Run, source routing restrictions and loader departures. Numerical readiness and researcher approval were not established.
fields.Model extraction:
Source fidelity is supported by retained source reconciliation and round-trip checks. Missing source inputs were completed only from deposited Rpath outputs: biomass for 8 groups, Q/B for 11 and EE for 61. No new biological solve supplied these values.
Source diets were not normalized. Native unassimilated fractions and explicit zero biomass accumulation were retained. Three all-zero detritus-fate rows fail the generic importer sum rule. The deposited static living and detritus budgets balance, with five P/Q range warnings.
The recorded loader drops phytoplankton routing to the two natural detritus pools, adds detritus self-routing and drops source TLs to missing values. These runtime departures are distinct from source balance and require explicit interpretation in the diagnostic result.
The constructed runtime has negative detritus stock residuals: DOM −609.88, POM −806.82 and Discards −0.4959 t/km²/year. These are runtime residuals, not the source’s explicit zero biomass accumulation.

fields.Temporal fit: Static base state: 1991; the report's time-series calibration spans 1991–2013. Applying the port to 2019 catch is a 28-year transfer of the baseline food web, not a calibrated 2019 reconstruction. A future fixed allocation would need its own temporal justification.
fields.Other:
Diagnostics apply to a separate runtime convention: four undefined synthetic-import diet cells for nonfeeding groups 66–69 were set to structural zero. These zeros are operational, not observed source values. The unmodified loader attempt raised a detritus-column exception; both attempts are retained.
EE floor 0.1 creates a hypothetical external nonfishery sink of 1.9837 t/km²/year across eight living groups; source EE remains unchanged. No diet normalization or post-normalization BA balancing was applied. The PPR budget gap matches the unrouted phytoplankton mortality, consistent with a runtime accounting limitation. With Egestion also returned FAIL. No exact-model regional taxon mapping is retained.

recommendation: Recommend the East Coast of Scotland 1991–1995 model as the interim selection for further review between these two implementations. It has saved GE and With Egestion results graded OK and a retained regional mapping; the tested ICES runtime failed all three methods. Scotland remains a subregional proxy, its TE result fails, and its snapshot provenance prevents automatic numerical restoration. Neither candidate currently supports an unqualified validated whole-North-Sea PPR estimate.

comparison_note: This is a comparison of available evidence, not a test under common settings: Scotland diagnostics are historical configured outcomes; ICES uses the current EE floor and the stated structural-zero convention. The failures do not establish that the deposited ICES source model is intrinsically worse. Neither candidate has a registered researcher decision. Three other registered models were screened only: Scotland 1890–1895 and two Mackinson 2007 representations.
geography_intro: R is the North Sea LME. S is the union of official ICES divisions IVa, IVb and IVc, reconstructed from the area statement in Annex 6. It is a proxy for the modeled domain, not a model-specific boundary polygon, which was not supplied.
map_caption: Figure 1. Repository LME_022 boundary and official ICES division union in a common equal-area display. WGS84 geodesic intersection gives A = 86.53% and B = 98.86%; applying a common Natural Earth 1:50 million land mask gives A = 87.14% and B = 99.63%. These boundary treatments support the approximate ranges in the main table.
source_caption: Figure 2. ICES WGSAM report, Annex 6, printed page 102 / PDF page 104. The area statement identifies North Sea ICES divisions IVa, IVb and IVc; the stated time range describes the report calibration rather than a 2019 base model.
geography_limit: The study-domain map above is this review's geographic reconstruction. No model-specific boundary polygon was supplied or recovered. The downloaded official divisions are not an archived model-period boundary. Differences in northern and eastern boundaries and coastline resolution prevent treating the estimate as exact coverage of the native model.
